name: Nevada
overview: Nevada does not sell tax liens. When real property taxes go unpaid, the county tax receiver issues a certificate that lets the county treasurer hold the property as trustee for the State and county for 2 years after the first Monday in June of the year the certificate is dated, unless it is redeemed sooner. Interest is added to the unpaid taxes at 10 percent per annum, assessed monthly, until paid. If the property is not redeemed, the tax receiver deeds it to the county treasurer as trustee, and the board of county commissioners can direct the treasurer to sell it after giving notice of sale, so buyers at these auctions get the property itself.

counties.schedule_rule: The Treasurer's Office may conduct at least one tax auction per year, usually in Spring.

counties.how_to_bid: Register online through the Treasurer's Real Property Tax Auction page or in person at the Treasurer's Office, with a $5,000.00 registration deposit per bidder in certified funds (cash, cashier's check, wire or money order). Registration is limited to 280 bidders. Only the registered bidder may bid, showing a bidder card; parcels are offered one at a time in the order of the published list. Pay in full at the Treasurer's Office by the stated time. There is no redemption period after the auction; properties are sold as is.
